asr.full_text: So once you've registered with a Bit Club network and you've paid your joining fee, you need to start earning the Bitcoin. So to enable you to do that, you need to purchase a share in one of the pools, the Mining pools. So on the welcome page here if we log in if you scroll down to here, these are the three pools available, pool one ,pool two, and pool three. Or you can buy a founder pool which means you'll get one share in each of these pools, pool one, pool 2 and pool 3. So, I'm going to go over that in a little bit more detail in just a moment. So also from time to time when you log in, you will see these additional GPU mining pools offers appearing. These are for mining other coins such as ethereum. And they come on a first come first serve base. They are not always available in your back office so when you see them, if it's something you wanna participate in, then you need to snap them up while they're available. So we'll come back to that in a moment. So back to the main mining pools. So let's take a look at this and explain exactly how it works and how to choose your pool. Okay, so the BITclub network has thousands and thousands of machines mining bitcoin every day and these machines are split up across these three pools So if you buy a share in pool one, which is the lowest cost of $500 you get thousand days mining. So this will be earning you bitcoin every day for a thousand days initially. Fifty percent of that bitcoin earned is split between the shareholders which would be you, and fifty percent is put back into repurchase. And the reason for the repurchase is that with the speed and technology of AsicChips and the mining equipment changing on a constant basis, then the Bitclub Networks need to upgrade and needs to buy new machines or upgrade the equipment in order to keep the mining pools running as efficiently as possible. So, when you purchase a $500 share in this pool, 50% of your Commission's would be paid into your Bitcoin wallet and 50% will be used to repurchase. So what that also means is that these repurchases come back to you as partial shares and these partial shares are up to become full shares over time. So that 1000 day mining you get initially from one share is three and a half years or more mining but in reality it never expires because as these repurchases come into play and get activated, so they start from another 1000 days and as one share is coming to an end, you've still got other shares running and which started at a later date. So all three pools work on a very similar basis, you get 1000 days mining ,only with pool two you get 60 percent commission paid your Bitcoin wallet and forty percent is used to repurchase and pool three is 70% commission and a 30% repurchase but also in another video I'll be showing you how you can change the repurchase to a hundred percent or other amounts if you want to which means that you get more shares faster so then you've also got the founder pool. Now the founder pool gives you one share in each of these pools pool one pool two and pool three and also comes with some other bonuses and special offers. And these include some things like shares in the Coin Pay. Coin Pay is a merchant acquisition application, which allows businesses to accept Bitcoin and Coin Pay will charge a 1% fee on all the transactions used to collect the Bitcoin. And those 1% fees will then be shared with the shareholders in coin pay So that's one of the benefits of a founder member You actually get a small share in the coin pay and the bit club network actually has his own coin as well It is called a club coin and the club coin was created as it as a reward token for all bit club network members And they've already given away over 60 million club coins to members for free and you can actually check this on bitrex.com where club coin is actually trading live and that's another way you can actually check any cryptocurrency to see if it's actually real if it's not trading on Bitrex or some of the other trading websites then it's not a real coin so that's some of the benefits of the founder pool. So choose your shares according to your budget and what you can actually afford. I mean, if you can afford the founder pool then I recommend it but otherwise you might wanna go with one of the other pools. So in order to purchase share in any of these pools, you need to click the Buy Now and BICCLUB only accepts Bitcoins so you need to make sure that you do have enough Bitcoin in your external Bitcoin wallet to cover this. So when you click buy now for example on the 500 pool one, an invoice will be generated and you have 10 minutes to pay the invoice via Bitcoin before the invoice expires, so again the same way as we use the registration fee or the joining fee for the Bit Club network So again we can send in your Bitcoin payment to the address given here and the amount in btc. So you copy the amount you need to send and the address to send it to, and When you make that payment you will then have the shares show up in your account once it's processed. So once that is processed and the share shows up in your account. Then once you have your shares, when you register for the Bitcoin payment. You will receive your payment information which the shares show up in your account once it's processed so once that is processed on the share shows up in your account it's going to show as pending first with 1010 or 1030 days which will count down each day until it gets set up completely from 1 0 days down it will be in a new bitcoin and this is explained a little bit more in the next video also so let's move on and i'll see you in

textual.observation: The speaker promotes paying a joining fee and purchasing mining-pool shares, describing a $500 pool share as providing Bitcoin mining for 1,000 days and daily Bitcoin earnings, with part of the earnings paid to the participant and part reused to purchase additional shares.

evidence.quote: once you've registered with a Bit Club network and you've paid your joining fee, you need to start earning the Bitcoin
if you buy a share in pool one, which is the lowest cost of $500 you get thousand days mining
50% of your Commission's would be paid into your Bitcoin wallet and 50% will be used to repurchase

textual.context: Instructional and promotional presentation of how to purchase and use mining-pool shares; the source does not establish whether the described earnings occurred.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised Bitcoin return is directly linked to paying a joining fee and purchasing a $500 mining-pool share, with additional share accumulation described as a result of the repurchase mechanism.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish the actual operation, legitimacy, profitability, or payment history of the program, nor whether participants received the described returns.

textual.observation: The speaker urges viewers to act quickly when additional GPU mining-pool offers appear, stating that availability is limited and that viewers should obtain them while available.

evidence.quote: They are not always available in your back office so when you see them, if it's something you wanna participate in, then you need to snap them up while they're available

textual.context: Presented as promotional guidance within an instructional walkthrough; the source does not clarify whether the availability limitation was independently verified.
textual.potential_relevance: A time- or availability-sensitive instruction is linked to participating in additional mining pools and the associated described mining benefits.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish the actual supply, deadline, or consequences of not acting quickly.

textual.observation: The speaker directs viewers to fund a pool-share purchase using Bitcoin from an external wallet, copy a payment address and BTC amount, and pay a generated invoice within 10 minutes before it expires.

you have 10 minutes to pay the invoice via Bitcoin before the invoice expires

textual.context: Step-by-step payment instructions in a promotional purchase tutorial; the source does not establish whether the payment address or transaction outcome was verified.
textual.potential_relevance: A Bitcoin transfer to a supplied payment address is required to obtain the promoted pool shares, with a short invoice-expiration condition attached to the payment.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish the recipient identity, transaction completion, wallet ownership, or whether shares were actually credited after payment.

visual.observation: A website presents Bitcoin mining pool packages priced at $500, $1,000, $2,000, and $3,500 with a “Buy Now” action, 1,000 days of mining, stated commission percentages, and re-purchase terms.
visual.context: Promotional commercial webpage; the supplied frames do not establish whether the stated mining, commission, or re-purchase outcomes occurred.
visual.potential_relevance: A promised financial return or benefit is presented in connection with purchasing a cryptocurrency mining package, which conditionally merits review of the offer and payment arrangement.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish the provider's identity, the underlying mining activity, whether buyers received the stated benefits, or any resulting loss.

visual.observation: An invoice page displays a Bitcoin payment amount, a recipient address, a QR code, and instructions to pay; it states that the payment is valid for 10 minutes and warns that payment after expiration may not be paid or that Bitcoin may not be returned.
visual.context: The page visibly provides cryptocurrency payment instructions and an expiration condition; the full address and QR contents are not transcribed.
visual.potential_relevance: A requested cryptocurrency transfer is linked to a short payment deadline and stated consequences for late payment, creating a conditionally relevant payment-flow cue.
visual.limitations: The frames cannot establish whether a payment was made, who controlled the destination, whether the invoice was valid, or whether any funds were lost.

visual.observation: The payment page shows “Pay with Bitcoin” and a BTC-denominated amount, while a red overlaid notice states that BitClub only accepts Bitcoin Cash payments because of Bitcoin fees and that Bitcoin can be converted into Bitcoin Cash.
visual.context: The Bitcoin Cash statement appears as a prominent red overlay across the sampled webpage; the frames do not clarify whether it is webpage content, video annotation, or a time-specific instruction.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible payment instructions and the overlaid currency statement describe different cryptocurrency payment methods, so the supplied frames conditionally merit review for payment-method consistency.
visual.limitations: Sparse samples cannot establish the intended current payment method, whether the overlay applies to the invoice, or whether the two currencies could be converted through a stated process.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes pool shares as a way to earn Bitcoin, including a $500 share described as providing daily earnings for 1,000 days, and recommends the higher-priced Founder Pool. It directs prospective buyers to fund the purchase from an external Bitcoin wallet, send payment to a displayed address, and meet a 10-minute invoice deadline while urging them to take available offers. The claims and payment instructions are described, but mining activity, actual returns, and completed payment are not verified.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The speaker links buying a mining-pool share to recurring Bitcoin earnings and describes commissions paid to a wallet, with a portion used to repurchase shares. The displayed offers provide a purchase pathway. The share price is mining participation capital, not a fee for earning guidance.
